english.notes:
(i) This offence should not be used from 28th September 2026 due to changes made by section 113 of the Crime and Policing Act 2026. The amended offences will also capture those who expose their genitals with the intent to cause humiliation to those who may see them (as well as alarm and distress), or those who do so for the purposes of obtaining sexual gratification while being reckless as to whether someone who sees them will be caused alarm, distress or humiliation. For the offences applying after this date, see H102884 and H102885.(ii) It is not necessary for the defendant's genitals to have been seen by anyone or for anyone to have been alarmed or distressed. For example, if a person exposes his genitals to some passers-by, he may (depending on his state of mind) commit the offence regardless of whether they actually see his genitals or whether they have been alarmed or distressed by seeing them.(iii) The offence would not apply to a naturist who intentionally exposes his genitals in the knowledge that they may be seen by others but without the intention to cause alarm or distress. Similarly, it would exclude an exhibitionist streaker at a sports occasion. For further guidance in relation to such a case, please see the CPS Guidance: Nudity in Public – Guidance on handling cases of Naturism and the College of Policing Briefing Note: Public nudity advice and decision aid.(iv) "Genitals" refers to male or female sexual organs.(v) This offence, where the victim or intended victim was under 18 at the time of the offence, is listed as a child sex offence in paragraph 10 of Schedule 34A to the Criminal Justice Act 2003 for the purposes of disclosing information relating to convictions for such offences to members of the public under section 327A (Sarah’s law).(vi) A person convicted of this offence is subject to notification and orders as provided by section 80 of the Act as follows -
(a) where the offender was under 18 years of age where he is or has been sentenced in respect of the offence to imprisonment for a term of at least 12 months;
(b) in any other case, the victim was under 18 or the offender in respect of the offence or finding, is or has been sentenced to a term of imprisonment, detained in a hospital, or made the subject of a community sentence of at least 12 months. (Sch 3 paragraph 33).

other.penalty:
Either waySummary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment. This is a specified child sex offence; where this offence is aggravated by grooming and the victim or intended victim was under the age of 18, see section 70A of the Sentencing Act 2020.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.
Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
